GeometryCirclesConstructions
Game: This picture shows a circle, a line across it, and two short lines that always turn out the same length.
How to play: Drag the dots: O moves the circle, the dot beside it changes its size, and C and D swing the line. Use the buttons to show the names, the claim, or a hint.
Look for the math

Here is a small surprise from Archimedes' Book of Lemmas: however you tilt a chord of a circle, two lengths drawn from the ends of a diameter stay equal.

What the page claims

Let AB be a diameter and let a chord CD (not a diameter) meet it in E. Draw AM and BN perpendicular to the chord. Proposition 13 says:

CN = DM.

The logic test checks this at the starting picture, on a grid of chord directions, and on 600 random circles and chords. It holds for every chord that is not a diameter.

The centre cuts the chord in half

Drop OH perpendicular to CD from the centre O. The line from the centre perpendicular to a chord always cuts it in two equal pieces, so CH = HD. The E where the chord crosses the diameter can sit outside the circle; that makes no difference, because the construction only uses the two whole lines.

Two midpoints in a row

Join B to M and carry the line HO until it meets BM at K. Since O is the midpoint of AB and HO runs parallel to AM, the midpoint theorem gives BK = KM. In the same way, the line through that midpoint parallel to the two perpendiculars meets MN at its midpoint, so NH = HM.

Subtract equal pieces

Now the chord is balanced twice: CH = HD and NH = HM. Taking the pieces between C and N and between D and M leaves the same length, so CN = DM. Another way to see it is to measure distances along the chord from H: C and D sit at +a and -a, while M and N sit at -b and +b, because O is midway between A and B. Both CN and DM are |a - b|.

One small quirk of the old applet is kept here: when a foot lands within about 0.3 units of C, its 0.1 squared-distance shortcut returns C's neighbour unmoved, so the drawn segments can differ by a hair. With exact feet the equality is exact; the test checks both.

Turn the hint on and drag D almost opposite C: when the chord becomes a diameter the whole construction disappears, just as it does in the applet.
